chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), regarding

a contracted slave who died, having paid a portion of his manumission amount, and left wealth, and he had two free children. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'His wealth is to be distributed among them by shares.'
ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a deceased contracted slave divided among his free children according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that a mukatab’s estate is treated as free property for inheritance purposes, with the remaining wealth distributed equally among his free children. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that the slave’s status does not hinder the transmission of wealth to his offspring, reflecting the principle of equity in familial inheritance rights.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) regarding

a contracted slave who died and he had paid off something from his contracted amount, and left wealth, and for him were two free children. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Make his wealth to be between them with the quotas’.
